question.text: How many shrimp per year will be covered by SWP's Humane Slaughter Initiative agreements on July 1, 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the Shrimp Welfare Project's estimated "[Shrimpact](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)" (in billions of shrimp helped in expectation per year) when checked by Metaculus on or soon after July 1, 2027.
question.fine_print:
The question will resolve as the headline estimated Shrimpact, regardless of any estimated range. If SWP ceases to provide a headline estimate and instead provides only a range, however, the question will resolve as the midpoint of the range.

The total Shrimpact will be rounded, if necessary, to the nearest 100 million shrimp.

research:
I'm done researching and am writing up the findings.

## 1. Resolution source

- **2026-11-19:** The [Shrimpact page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact) shows a headline of **6,400,000,000** shrimp helped in expectation per year, with a range of 4.5B to 9.0B. It reports 37 agreements in 9 countries covering 89,773 MT per year. Of these, 22 stunners are installed and commissioned, covering 56,974 MT (about 4.1B shrimp). By country: Vietnam about 2.54B, Honduras 1.30B, India 0.63B, Indonesia 0.57B, Ecuador 0.48B, Sri Lanka 0.44B, Venezuela 0.28B, Thailand 0.18B, Nigeria 0.072B. The country figures add up to about 6.49B, slightly more than the headline.
- The page's FAQ says the headline is "committed impact" from signed agreements, whether or not the stunner is installed yet. Retailer policies are not counted. It is just a number on the page: I found no data file or API behind it.

## 2. Current status

- Nothing is settled yet. The current 6.4B is **below the question's lower bound of 6.95B**, so roughly another 0.6B or more must be added by July 1, 2027 for the result to land inside the range.
- The headline can go down as well as up. It read 6.5B on 2026-10-25 and 6.4B now. Committed tonnage was essentially the same (89,774 MT then, 89,773 MT now), but the installed count rose from 20 to 22, so the drop looks like a change in how tonnes are converted to shrimp numbers. [Wayback 2026-10-25](http://web.archive.org/web/20261025070430/https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- **2026-11-13:** Animal Charity Evaluators (ACE) named SWP a Recommended Charity for the fourth year running. The press release gives no new agreement figures. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/press-release-ace-recommended-charity-2026)
- **2026-10-08 to 2026-10-25:** Agreements went from 36 to 37 and tonnage from 86,875 to 89,774 MT. Honduras rose from 1.09B to 1.30B and the headline from 6.3B to 6.5B. [Wayback 10-08](http://web.archive.org/web/20261008223907/https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- **2026-08:** Albert Heijn and Confremarca announced a pilot where SWP tracks stunner use through a database. A search summary says an ACE evaluation from August 2026 put coverage at about 6.1B; I did not verify that. [Shrimp Insights](https://www.shrimpinsights.com/advertorial/future-shrimp-welfare-how-retailers-can-validate-electrical-stunning-commitments)
- **2026-01-14:** Trang Corporation committed to stun 1,800 MT per year. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/trangs-group-trang-corporation-dary-foods-join-humane-slaughter-partnership-with-shrimp-welfare-project)
- **2025-12-01:** C.P. Viet Nam committed to stun all vannamei shrimp for the UK market from 2026-01-01. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/cpvietnam-westbridge-food-group-join-shrimp-welfare-project-electrical-stunning-programme)
- **2025-09-16:** The 21st agreement (CAMIMEX) brought the estimate to about 4B. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/major-milestone-for-humane-slaughter-shrimp-welfare-project-expected-to-help-4-billion-shrimps-annually-new-mou-with-camimex-seafood-connection)
- SWP has published no individual press release for a new agreement since January 2026, even though the count went from about 30 to 37. New agreements seem to show up on the page without an announcement. [SWP blog](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog)

## 4. Base rates and history of the headline (Wayback snapshots)

- 2024-01-01: 1.2B
- 2024-07-17: 2.2B
- 2025-01-05: 2.8B
- 2025-07-21: 3.8B
- 2025-10-22 and 2025-11-13: 4.5B
- 2026-01-10 to 2026-03-07: 5.4B
- 2026-08-20: 6.1B
- 2026-09-17 and 2026-10-08: 6.3B
- 2026-10-25: 6.5B
- 2026-11-19: 6.4B

[CDX index](http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact&output=txt&collapse=digest&fl=timestamp,digest)

- **Same window in earlier years (mid-November to early July):**
  - 2024-25: from about 2.6B (interpolated) to 3.8B, roughly +1.2B
  - 2025-26: from 4.5B to about 6.0B (6.1B in August), roughly +1.5B
- **Growth rate:** about 1.6 to 2.0B per year in 2025 and 2026. It came in steps, with long flat stretches such as January to March 2026 and October to November 2025.
- **Pace slowing:** from 2026-03 to 2026-11 the headline rose only about 1.0B in 8 months, slower than before.
- **Seasonality:** none apparent. Changes follow when agreements are signed, not the farming calendar.
- **Possible one-off jump:** older pages marked India with "SSFI impact to be added after our Pilot phase". That note had disappeared by October 2026, and I could not confirm whether SSFI (SWP's Sustainable Shrimp Farming in India programme) is now included.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question (turkey slaughter, trade deals and so on) are related.
- SWP's long-term goal is to help 100B shrimp by 2030, but it gives no number for 2027. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimp)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- New agreements, which are typically about 2,000 MT each (roughly 0.1 to 0.2B shrimp), signed with a buyer as co-signatory. [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/aquaculture/uk-nonprofit-ensuring-viability-of-shrimp-welfare-commitments-through-electrical-stunner-agreements)
- Possible changes to the tonnes-to-shrimp conversion. These have already moved the headline down by 0.1B.
- SSFI India impact possibly being added.
- Possible methodology changes as SWP builds out "verified use" monitoring. That could lower the headline or change what it measures.
- Year-end giving season in December, and the monthly newsletters.
- Weather is not relevant.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-19: The [SWP (Shr)Impact page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact) shows a headline of **6,400,000,000 shrimp helped in expectation each year**, with a range of 4.5 to 9.0 billion and about 1,400 shrimp per dollar.
  - It counts 37 corporate agreements across 9 countries, covering 89,773 MT per year once all stunners are working.
  - 22 stunners are installed and commissioned, covering 56,974 MT, or about 4.1 billion shrimp.

- The page says the figure converts committed annual tonnage into a number of shrimp. It covers all signed agreements, including stunners not yet delivered, and does not count retailer commitments. I found no underlying data file; the page is static Squarespace HTML.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The headline needs to grow by about 0.55 billion or more (about 9%) to reach the lower bound of the range.
- 2026-10-25: The page showed **6.5B** for 37 agreements and 89,774 MT. By 2026-11-19 it showed **6.4B** for essentially the same tonnage. That points to a small change in how tonnage is converted to shrimp, not lost agreements. The country figures on today's page still add up to about 6.49B. ([Wayback](https://web.archive.org/web/20261025070430/https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact))
- The current figure works out to about 71,000 shrimp per MT. On that basis, roughly 7,700 more MT (about 4 typical MOUs of about 2,000 MT each) would be needed to reach 6.95B.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Animal Charity Evaluators (ACE) named SWP a Recommended Charity for the fourth year in a row. ([SWP blog](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog))

Other patterns:
- The series rises in steps, often flat for months (Jan to Mar 2026, Sep to Oct 2026).
- It has dipped slightly only once (6.5B to 6.4B, a recalibration).
- Seasonality: none obvious. Changes depend on when MOUs are signed.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the collected Kalshi markets match this question. They cover turkey slaughter, trade deals and similar topics.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on SWP's Shrimpact, and I could not see the Metaculus community forecast.
- ACE's earlier review says SWP could usefully spend about $3.6M a year in 2026 and 2027. Planned uses include a cheaper stunner, third-party checking and reserves to deploy many stunners if an opportunity arises. ACE gives no numeric stunner targets. ([ACE](https://animalcharityevaluators.org/charity-review/shrimp-welfare-project/))

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- New MOUs, each typically requiring a commitment of about 1,900 to 2,000 MT per year with a buyer co-signing. Vietnam, India, Indonesia and Latin America have been the active markets. ([HSI page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/humane-slaughter-initiative))
- Possible further changes to the conversion method. The November 2026 tweak lowered the figure by 0.1B. The new "verified use" category might eventually change what the headline counts.
- A cheaper stunner, or the reserves for deploying many stunners at once, could speed up signings.
- Donations around Giving Tuesday and year-end after the ACE recommendation could affect how many stunners SWP can fund.
- Weather is not relevant to this question.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 7.4 months until the July 1, 2027 check. Forecasts close June 1, 2027.

(b) **Latest known value:** 6.4B shrimp per year (range 4.5B to 9.0B), from 37 agreements, as of 2026-11-19.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 6,400,000,000.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- Same-window growth in earlier years was +1.2B (2024-25) and +1.5B (2025-26).
- The more recent pace has slowed to about 1.0B per 8 months, which implies roughly +0.8 to +1.0B by July 2027.
- That gives about 7.2 to 7.5B.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Over about 7 months, the headline has moved between roughly +0.7B and +1.5B.
- It moves in steps, with flat stretches of 2 to 3 months.
- It has also dropped slightly (by 0.1B) from conversion changes.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There are no markets on this. SWP's long-term goal is 100B by 2030, but it gives no figure for 2027. The question creator expects roughly 7B to 12B, which looks somewhat optimistic given the slowing pace.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** SWP switches the headline to "verified use" or installed-only impact, which would be about 4.1B or less. A conversion revision or a partner withdrawing could also cut it.
- **High:** SSFI India impact gets added, or a very large producer signs (for example an Ecuadorian or Indian exporter, or an expanded CP group commitment), adding 2B or more.

(f) Experts and markets: there are no markets on this. The question creator's range of 7 to 12B suggests they expect continued growth. Animal Charity Evaluators (ACE) gives no numeric targets.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** MOU signings stall (funding, stunner supply, or SWP shifting toward checking that stunners are actually used). SWP could also recalibrate the shrimp-per-MT conversion again, or start counting only verified or commissioned stunners. The commissioned stunners alone come to about 4.1B, so a switch to counting only those is the 1st-percentile tail. Partial methodology tightening is more plausible and gives about 6.0 to 6.4B.
- **High:** a cheaper stunner or the reserve fund unlocks a large batch of deployments. Alternatively, one or two very large producers in Ecuador or India sign agreements of 10,000 MT or more, or retailer-driven commitments spread quickly. Any of these would push the figure above 9.5 to 10B, the 99th-percentile tail.
